preregistration.summary: Recomputed from the pack before opening runs/. Child support (Worksheet A, two children): salary-only H net 10,920 + W net 4,680 = 15,600 -> basic 3,050 -> H share 2,135.00 (the proposal's basis); with the HR-letter bonus H gross 213,000 -> net 13,845, combined 18,525 -> 3,050 -> H share 2,279.47. If the guideline maintenance adjustment is applied (2,000/mo): gross-level method gives 2,022.63, net-level method gives 1,950.19; both are acceptable per the manifest if the method is stated. After-tax split: wife house = 1,100,000 - 66,000 costs - 400,000 mortgage - 18.8% x (734,000 - 250,000) = 543,008; plus 70,000 = 613,008. Husband = 400,000 x 0.76 + (300,000 - 15% x 80,000) + 70,000 = 662,000 (658,960 if NIIT is also applied to the brokerage gain). Wife < husband holds under every sensitivity (no-NIIT 631,400; 401(k) at 32% -> 630,000; joint 500k exclusion -> 660,008). Pre-decree joint sale saves 47,000 (90,992 -> 43,992). YTD stub excess = 146,212 - 119,000 = 27,212. Key agrees with my figures on every item.

cross_run_observations: No trust-fatal events in any run; every cited authority in all five final deliverables resolves to a library/INDEX.md file. All five runs caught all six traps before the review turn (unprompted); B's §121-timing catch is a single unquantified sentence. Oracle: A and C report the undisclosed bonus as 50,400 (45,000 x 112% of plan) and fail the +/-5,000 amount check by 400 while stating 45,000 as the floor — a fixture-tolerance question rather than a substantive miss. B is the only run whose division.json instruments omit the QDRO (its alternatives avoid the 401(k); advice.md still explains the QDRO requirement). All five applied the guideline maintenance adjustment with a stated method (2,022.63 at the 45,000 bonus; 2,041.74–2,042 at 50,400), and B and D also report the 2,279.47 no-adjustment figure. Four runs (A, C, D, E) independently proposed a deferred co-owned sale using §121(d)(3)(A) to preserve two 250,000 exclusions without a joint return; the reference lists only the pre-decree joint sale, so this is an extension of the key that the library text supports. Review turns were genuinely useful in A (40,000-per-side cash error), C (unsupported custody-factor attribution and an invented trigger date), D (interest figure) and E (displayed fraction, conditional NIIT edge); B's review changed wording only. D is the only run that converted the client's 'I don't know if I can refinance' into 'client says she cannot refinance'; graded as a non-fatal mischaracterisation with medium confidence. Only C asked the overnights question; the other four relied on the schedule's ~70/30 and reached the same custodial-parent conclusion.
